headline: Chips Surge 5.2% While Most Stocks Slip as Money Rotates Out of Software and Housing
body_html:
Semiconductors dominated Friday's session, jumping 5.23% as the AI build-out trade came back with force. Hassett's argument that a Democratic wave in Washington would not stop data center construction gave the group a supportive backdrop, even as talk of an AI sell-off and fading odds on a marquee AI listing hung over the tape.

Beneath that rally, the market was far less cheerful. Of the 525 stocks we track, 236 rose and 287 fell. Money moved out of homebuilders (down 2.10%), consumer names (down 1.63%) and software (down 1.54%), and into energy (up 0.99%) and materials (up 0.31%). Industrials were essentially flat at +0.09%, and healthcare eased 0.15%.

The chip rally reached well beyond the biggest names. Alpha and Omega Semiconductor soared 27.76%, and Diodes added 13.17%. Networking and optical suppliers followed, with Ubiquiti up 15.29%, Extreme Networks up 14.16% and Coherent up 13.58%. TransMedics topped the board at 27.92%, while BlackLine fell 23.11%. A single group did the heavy lifting for the indexes while most stocks declined. Monday, November 9, will show whether the buying can broaden.

briefs.headline: Chip Group Posts the Session's Biggest Sector Gain
briefs.body: Semiconductors climbed 5.23%, far ahead of every other group we track. Energy was next at 0.99%. The gap shows how concentrated Friday's buying was, with the AI hardware complex absorbing most of the enthusiasm.

briefs.headline: Networking and Optical Names Ride the Data Center Wave
briefs.body: Ubiquiti rose 15.29%, Extreme Networks gained 14.16% and Coherent advanced 13.58%. The jumps came as commentary stressed that AI infrastructure spending would continue despite the political shift in Washington. Buyers favored the equipment that connects the servers.

briefs.headline: BlackLine Sinks Over 23% as Software Slides
briefs.body: BlackLine dropped 23.11%, the steepest decline on our board, and the software group lost 1.54% overall. Capital seemed to leave application software for hardware. The sector now looks like the funding source for the chip rally.

briefs.headline: Housing and Consumer Shares Take the Brunt
briefs.body: Homebuilders fell 2.10% and consumer stocks lost 1.63%, the two weakest groups of the day. Brokerage firm eXp World Holdings slid 20.72% and flooring maker Interface dropped 18.72%. Housing-linked names took the sharpest hits.

briefs.headline: Healthcare Splits Between a Big Winner and Big Losers
briefs.body: The sector slipped only 0.15%, but the stock moves were dramatic. TransMedics jumped 27.92%, while Artivion fell 20.21% and Natera lost 14.59%. Stock-specific news mattered far more than any sector trend.

briefs.headline: Energy and Materials Hold Modest Gains in a Fearful Tape
briefs.body: Energy added 0.99% and materials rose 0.31% while fewer than half of tracked stocks advanced. Commentary urged investors to stay the course and watch for buying chances, and one report said the market's fear gauge may be signaling a bottom. Cyclical groups offered a quieter refuge.
